blocks.text: A limit must agree along every admissible approach. Different path limits disprove existence. Agreement on a few paths does not prove existence.

items.title: Different axis limits
paragraphs: Along x=0 the ratio is 1. Along y=0 it is −1. Both paths approach the origin inside the punctured domain.
These two path limits disagree, so no common two-variable limit exists.

items.title: Slope-dependent rational function
question_paragraphs: Show that \(xy/(y^2-x^2)\) has no limit as \((x,y)\to(0,0)\).
paragraphs: Taking m=0 gives zero; taking m=2 gives 2/3. These two admissible paths have different limits.

items.title: Question and working use different denominators
question_paragraphs: The notebook question is \(f(x,y)=xy^2/(x^2+y^2)\) at (0,0). Its working instead uses \(g(x,y)=xy^2/(x^2+y^4)\). Discuss both.
paragraphs: For the question as written, \(|xy^2/(x^2+y^2)|\le|x|\). As (x,y)→(0,0), the right side tends to zero, so the limit is zero by squeezing.
For the denominator used in the class working, axes give zero and the line y=mx also gives zero, but these paths do not establish existence.
Along the curved path x=my², \(g=my^4/[(m^2+1)y^4]=m/(m^2+1)\). For m=1 this is 1/2, disagreeing with the axis limit zero.
items.final_answer: The written question has limit 0. The function used in the working has no limit.
